quote: Human evaluation remains the gold standard to determine the quality of texts generated by Natural Language Generation (NLG) systems.
We evaluate a total of 15 data-to-text systems, comprising three rule-based systems and 12 neural systems, of which two are large language models (LLMs) without any training or fine-tuning.

quote: we conducted our main evaluation study with 15 evaluators on 30 triples/verbalisation pairs for each evaluator.

We conducted a pilot experiment on a set of 10 triples/verbalisation pairs with 10 researchers from ADAPT Research Centre, Ireland. ... We used the brat annotation tool to record word‑span annotations of semantic errors (omission, addition, and repetition).

We invited researchers at the ADAPT Research Centre (Ireland) to participate in our study via an email (see email template in Appendix A) to the centre-wide mailing list, linking to a sign-up form that asked for English language proficiency...
guideline: The evaluator should check if each element in the input triples is verbalised. If any element is missing, it should be marked as an omission error...

The evaluator should check if each element in the input triples is verbalised (omission), if any content in the verbalisation does not correspond to an input element (addition), and if any content is repeated without a corresponding input repetition (repetition).

The evaluator should check if each element in the input triples is verbalised. If any element is missing, it should be marked as an omission error. ... The evaluator should check if all content words and phrases in the verbalisation correspond to elements in the triples. If any content word or phrase does not match an element in the triples, it should be marked as an addition error. ... The evaluator should check for repeated content in the output, including close paraphrases.
